In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the area under consideration the climate was drier in the past than today and wetter in the past than in the present semi-arid and desert zones.
in the Mediterranean zone the endolithic lichenes are the dominant weathering factor, whereas in the arid zones the blue-green algae are the main weathering agent.

the jigsaw-puzzle weathering pattern is a sign of a more humid climate than that which prevails today in the area where it is found, while deep pitting and channeling is indicative of more arid conditions than those prevailing today.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the weathering patterns observed in the field are the result of the interaction between climate and rock hardness, and that they can be used as palaeoclimatological indicators.
lichen and blue-green algal weathering patterns can be used as indicators of the past climate in areas with a semi-arid or arid climate.
in the Mediterranean zone lichens dominate the weathering of limestone and blue-green algae dominate the weathering in the semi-arid zone, whereas in the arid zone the blue-green algae are dominant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endolithic lichencolonies can be used as a bioindicator of the mean annual rainfall in the region.
the patterns of lichen and algae weathering on limestone surfaces provide a reliable indicator of past climate and can be used to reconstruct the palaeoclimate of arid and semi-arid zones.
the patterns of weathering by endolithic liches and by blue-green algae are sensitive palaeoclimatological indicators.
